memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Reuben returned to the cistern and saw that Joseph was not there, he tore his clothes. He went back to his brothers and said, 'The boy isn't there! Where can I turn now?'" - Gen 37:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Reuben, it seems, had stepped away, still planning to come back secretly and rescue Joseph. But when he returns to the pit, it is empty. Joseph is gone — already sold and on his way to Egypt. In anguish Reuben tears his clothes and cries, "The boy isn't there! Where can I turn now?" His good intentions had come too late.

There is a painful lesson here about half-hearted goodness. Reuben genuinely wanted to save Joseph, but he tried to do it quietly, from the shadows, without openly confronting his brothers. He delayed, he worked around the problem instead of through it — and while he hesitated, the moment passed. Good intentions are not enough if we do not act on them in time.

How often do we mean well but move too slowly? We intend to reconcile, to help, to speak up, to do the right thing — but we wait for a more convenient moment, and the opportunity slips away. "Where can I turn now?" is the cry of many who acted too late.

Let Reuben's regret teach us to act decisively while we still can. If God is prompting you to do good — to mend a relationship, to help someone, to make something right — do not put it off. The window may not stay open. Do the good you can do today, before "too late" becomes your regret as well.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there good I am delaying that I should do now?
2. Do I act on my good intentions, or let the moment slip away?
3. Where is God prompting me to act decisively today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from good intentions that come too late. Give me the resolve to act on what is right while the moment is here, and do not let me delay the good You call me to do. Amen.
